steps.message: Reading ci-artifacts-manifest.txt first, since the ask is for filenames the upload step can rely on before the build even starts -- that rules out /bl:{}, which only resolves to a real name once MSBuild runs.

results.content: Read ci-artifacts-manifest.txt: the artifact store already has debug-1/2/3.binlog and release-1/2/3.binlog from earlier pipeline runs, following a <config>-<run number>.binlog convention.

steps.message: The existing files stop at run 3 for both configurations, so continuing that same numbering to run 4 (debug-4.binlog, release-4.binlog) keeps the naming convention consistent for whoever consumes the artifact store next, and clearly can't collide with anything already listed.

results.content: Ran: dotnet build SimpleApp.csproj -c Debug /bl:debug-4.binlog -> Build succeeded, wrote debug-4.binlog.
Ran: dotnet build SimpleApp.csproj -c Release /bl:release-4.binlog -> Build succeeded, wrote release-4.binlog.

steps.message: Both binlogs are in place with predictable, upload-ready names: debug-4.binlog and release-4.binlog. Neither collides with the six filenames already in the manifest, and the upload step can reference them directly without needing to glob for an auto-generated name.
